guidance: Improper control settings may prevent the heater from reaching the desired temperature.
pitfalls: Ignoring inadequate heating may lead to fuel pump failures due to high viscosity.

condition: Minimum viscosity must be 2 cSt; maximum viscosity must not exceed 20 cSt.
guidance: Regular calibration ensures accurate readings for timely adjustments.
pitfalls: Failure to maintain proper viscosity can lead to fuel injection issues and engine stalling.

condition: All repairs must comply with classification society regulations.
guidance: Prompt fixing prevents further loss and maintains system integrity.
pitfalls: Ignoring leaks can result in fuel wastage and potential fire hazards.

condition: Flowmeter accuracy must be verified to ensure system reliability.
guidance: Physical issues can impede the accurate measurement of fuel flow.
pitfalls: Failure to address flowmeter issues can result in incorrect fuel dosing and operational inefficiencies.

condition: Circulating pump must maintain a pressure of 10 bar.
guidance: Air in the system can drastically affect pump performance.
pitfalls: Failure to address circulating pump issues can lead to engine overheating and stalling.

condition: Return line must allow for unimpeded fuel flow.
guidance: Restoring flow will relieve pressure and prevent system damage.
pitfalls: Failure to resolve blockages can lead to pressure-related failures and possible fuel leaks.

condition: Fuel oil must be free from water to ensure engine performance.
guidance: Effective separation will prevent future contamination.
pitfalls: Ignoring water contamination can result in engine failures and costly repairs.

condition: Separator must operate efficiently to meet ISO fuel quality standards.
guidance: Incorrect settings can reduce the separator's effectiveness.
pitfalls: Failure to maintain separator efficiency can lead to increased engine wear and operational issues.

condition: Transfer pump must be capable of maintaining flow rates as specified.
guidance: Blockages can prevent the pump from effectively moving fuel.
pitfalls: Ignoring pump failure can lead to fuel quality issues and engine performance degradation.

condition: Venting system must function to prevent pressure build-up.
guidance: Proper valve function is crucial for releasing excess pressure.
pitfalls: Ignoring this issue can lead to tank rupture and catastrophic failures.

condition: Fuel must be stored according to ISO standards to maintain quality.
guidance: Additives can help mitigate the effects of contamination.
pitfalls: Failure to maintain fuel quality can lead to engine performance issues and increased maintenance costs.

condition: Fuel oil pressure must be maintained within specified limits.
guidance: Leaks or faults can disrupt normal pressure regulation.
pitfalls: Ignoring pressure regulation issues can lead to severe engine performance problems.

condition: Regular maintenance must align with classification society requirements.
guidance: Regular maintenance will reduce the risk of future sludge accumulation.
pitfalls: Failure to manage sludge can lead to significant engine failures and costly repairs.

condition: Heating system must be functional to maintain fuel viscosity.
guidance: Damaged heating elements will not heat the fuel properly.
pitfalls: Ignoring this issue can lead to high viscosity and poor engine performance.

condition: Flushing must conform to manufacturer and classification society guidelines.
guidance: Record-keeping is essential for compliance and future reference.
pitfalls: Failure to flush can lead to severe contamination and engine damage.

condition: Filtration systems must comply with ISO standards for fuel cleanliness.
guidance: Upgrading can enhance fuel cleanliness and engine performance.
pitfalls: Ignoring high particulate levels can lead to significant engine wear and potential failures.
